name: web-browser
description: Control a real web browser to interact with JS-rendered pages, fill forms, navigate multi-step flows, and interact with sites that have no API. Use this instead of web-fetch when a page requires JavaScript, login, or user interaction. A call performs either ONE action (top-level `action`) or a SEQUENCE of actions in order against the same page (pass `actions`), then returns the updated page state (including content inside iframes, labelled '--- Frame: ... ---'). Pass session_id back on subsequent calls to maintain browser context across actions. BATCHING (`actions`): to fill a whole page of a long form in a SINGLE call, first get_content to read the element refs, then pass `actions` as an ordered list of steps like [{"action":"click","selector":"[g5f0e1]"},{"action":"click","selector":"[g5f0e2]"}, ... ,{"action":"click","selector":"Next"}] — each step has the same per-action fields (action, selector, text, value, key, url, secret_ref) minus the call-level ones (session_id/incognito/block_ads/screenshot apply to the whole batch). This turns a 60-question survey from ~69 calls into ~5, so it fits one turn budget instead of forcing the work to be split. Batch same-page actions (a page's answers + its Next click); after a page transition the old refs go stale, so end the batch at Next and get_content again on the next call. A batch stops at the first failed step and returns actions_completed/actions_total plus failed_action + action_error with fresh page content so you can recover. Actions: navigate (url required), click (selector required), type (selector + either text OR secret_ref), select (selector+value required), scroll (optional selector — scrolls that element into view, else scrolls the viewport down), hover (selector required — reveals hover-only menus/date cells), press_key (key required — e.g. Enter, Tab, ArrowRight, Escape; for calendar/combobox keyboard nav), wait_for (selector required — waits up to 10s for an element to render; use this for heavy widgets like date pickers that load after the page), get_content, screenshot, close_session (not allowed inside a batch). The page state lists interactable elements as '[gNfNeM] role "name"' under '--- Interactable elements ---'; prefer that gNfNeM ref as your selector (with or without the surrounding brackets — both resolve) — it targets exactly one element, so it is the reliable way to pick one option among duplicates (e.g. a survey row's repeated 'Agree'). A ref stays valid across later actions as long as its element is still on the page, so you can read once and act on several. Selectors that are not a ref still resolve by accessible role/label/text and aria-label and reach into iframes automatically; fall back to describing the element only when no ref fits (e.g. an element that appeared after the last snapshot). If an action reports that a ref is stale (the element is gone or the page re-rendered), call get_content to get fresh refs and use those — do not retry the old ref. If a click reports the target is covered or intercepted by another element (a sticky header/footer, cookie banner, ad, or modal sits over it), the browser auto-recenters and retries once; if it still fails, scroll the page or dismiss the blocking element (close the banner/modal), then retry. If several actions fail in a row the session may refuse further interactions (click/type/select/hover/wait_for) — get_content to re-read and recover, or hand off. Custom-styled widgets often hide the native input, and nearby visible caption text is frequently decorative rather than the clickable target. If a heavy widget (e.g. a date picker) seems missing, wait_for it before clicking. To fill a stored credential into a form, pass secret_ref (a user.* secret name) instead of text — the value is filled server-side and never shown to you. If navigate returns 'Site blocked automated access', the site refuses automation from the server; do not retry — hand off to the principal or draft the request instead. Set block_ads:true ONLY for plain content browsing — never for login, authenticated, or form-fill flows (sites flag the ad blocker as a privacy extension). Set incognito:true to run in a throwaway, isolated session (e.g. logging in as Curia itself) instead of the principal's persistent profile; omit it for the principal's own accounts so sessions persist. On bot-protected sites, prefer real UI interaction over injected fetch(). After navigate, the browser waits for Cloudflare-style challenge pages to clear automatically. RESUMING A SESSION: when you pass a session_id, check session_reused in the result — true means you reattached to the same live page; false means that session had expired and a fresh one was started, so re-navigate to your URL and continue from where you recorded you left off (don't assume the page is still mid-flow). LONG-RUNNING TASKS: if you're doing browser work you'll resume on a later wake (a multi-step flow you can't finish now), set keep_warm:true and record the returned session_id in the task's progress; the session then survives the idle window between wakes so you reattach to the same warm, logged-in page. Concurrent tasks each keep their own session and never collide.

inputs.action: string? (one browser action; required unless `actions` is given)
inputs.actions: object[]? (ordered list of {action, selector?, text?, value?, key?, url?, secret_ref?} steps run against the same page in one call; replaces the top-level action fields when present)
inputs.keep_warm: boolean? (pin this session so it survives between far-apart wakes; set it for a long task you will resume later, and record the session_id)

outputs.session_reused: boolean (true if a passed session_id reattached to its live session; false if it expired and a fresh session was started)
outputs.actions_total: number? (batch only: number of steps requested)
outputs.actions_completed: number? (batch only: number of steps that succeeded before any stop)
outputs.failed_action: number? (batch only: 0-based index of the step that failed, if any)
outputs.action_error: string? (batch only: why the failed step failed)
